status: Complete prepared residual-performance task binding for two specific and two affected overall records; no actual learner attainment, whole-source recertification or DB publication.

short: The class has a garden plan.
We will leave room for everyone to take part.
paragraph: Our group is making a small display about the garden. We need a clear title and readable notes. One drawing shows the path, and a caption explains it. We will ask a partner to check whether the message is clear.
extended: Our garden display has three parts: a plan, a picture and a short explanation. The plan shows where the paths go. The picture adds details about the available space. The explanation tells a visitor why the group chose this arrangement.

Before sharing, we will check the words and layout. If a partner misunderstands a detail, we will change it. We can compare the revised version with the earlier draft and explain how the change helps the reader.

protocol.setup: Use a suitable actual physical keyboard and word processor, a comfortable writing tool and the learned joined script. Record access arrangements, actual support and prior familiarity. Prepare unseen equivalent text for a later transfer; do not claim a familiar memorised copy establishes general fluency.
handwriting: Write a familiar two-line sample and common strings in the learned joined script; retain the older complete formation, size, spacing and joining checks separately.

Produce a new short dictated or own meaningful passage at a sustained comfortable pace. Check legibility with a willing reader and identify an actual useful adjustment; no child observation is supplied in this report.
keyboarding: On an actual suitable keyboard type the original short message, paragraph and extended text. Record which parts require repeated visual searching, interruptions to recall a key or adult prompting, and which proceed with increasingly ready retrieval. Accuracy and meaningful composition remain visible.

Review the actual output, correct genuine errors and explain a change that improves the message. Keep the untouched original result for comparison. Do not fabricate errors, successful key retrieval or improvement.

After appropriate practice, use a fresh equivalent message under comparable access conditions. Compare actual accuracy, continuity and independence with the earlier attempt, not with another child or a national speed norm. A supplied timed measure may describe the observation but creates no compulsory words-per-minute mastery threshold.
wordProcessing: For Grade5 choose readable fonts/size and suitable layout for the intended recipient, producing and enhancing each different-length message in the actual word processor. Explain a meaningful formatting choice rather than click an arbitrary font menu.

For Grade6 use the actual typing and revision evidence to explain whether the changed approach improves accuracy and communicative effect, with continuing fluency and more ready key retrieval distinguished from a single correct copied sentence.
protocol.closure: Combine actual fluent joined-script production, the relevant keyboard performance and purposeful word processing. A beginner home-row demonstration alone cannot discharge the later performance requirement. A worksheet, correct spelling answer or screenshot of finished text alone cannot establish automaticity.

gradeBindings.5: Initial emergence of ready keyboard retrieval across actual texts plus purposeful font/word-processing choices; no fixed speed cutoff.
gradeBindings.6: Increasing fluency, more ready retrieval and proficiency evidenced across comparable and fresh text with actual accuracy/effect; same operation, no separate tracked difficulty level.

limits: The blank template and prepared tasks are authoring resources, not successful observations or changes to learner estimates.
No broadening of Beginning touch typing, no new fluent-typing level/topic, no automatic transfer from handwriting fluency to keyboarding.
If suitable keyboard access or meaningful performance evidence is absent, keep the performance condition unassessed; inaccessible materials are not an assessed gap.
Existing D2 child writing/planning/revision/proofreading duties remain those of the accepted reports. Resolving this residual does not freshly recertify every historical Full judgment.
All eight data files and all historical reports remain unchanged.

historicalAcceptedContributions.remainingCondition: Keyboarding automaticity requires observed performance; topic links do not establish it.

performanceEvidence.positive: Actual joined-script production and keyboard use across the source-bound messages show the stated continuity, accuracy, meaningful correction and relevant tool choices. Grade-specific evidence is compared within the learner under recorded access/support.
performanceEvidence.nearMiss: A home-row picture, a perfect finished document copied by an adult, a memorised sentence or fluent pen writing without actual keyboard performance does not account for the keyboard duty.
performanceEvidence.transfer: Use a fresh meaningful text and a changed recipient/purpose, retain actual first output and corrections, and explain whether the revised approach supports accuracy and communication.
performanceEvidence.unassessed: No suitable keyboard, absent actual performance, inaccessible format or missing comparable attempts remains unassessed; it is not evidence of a child gap.
